item.title: AI skills not enough to level the playing field—study
item.description: Training in AI skills improves the chances of women from underrepresented backgrounds being invited to job interviews, but not enough to eliminate the inequalities they face in the labor market, according to a new study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Changes in DNA packaging help immune cells swell and burst
item.description: Immune cells are the elite athletes of the human body. While other cells stay in place, immune cells travel throughout our bodies, squeezing through small channels, stretching themselves, sampling the surfaces of other cells and swallowing up invaders. One of their most extreme behaviors is NETosis, a process in which certain immune cells burst and release their DNA as a way to trap pathogens. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: It took 10 billion years for this signal from the early universe to reach us
item.description: A newly discovered fast radio burst from 3 billion years after the big bang is among the most mysterious objects in astronomy. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Jacinta Bowler

item.title: More than half of LGBTQ+ adults in Massachusetts faced food insecurity in 2024
item.description: More than half of LGBTQ+ adults in Massachusetts experienced food insecurity in 2024, according to a new study published in JAMA Network Open. Researchers also found that food insecurity increased from 2022 to 2024 and remained significantly more common among LGBTQ+ adults than among non-LGBTQ+ adults. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New electrode design breaks key barrier to greener ammonia production
item.description: A new approach to producing ammonia using renewable electricity has overcome a fundamental energy limitation of the technology, opening new possibilities for cleaner and potentially more cost-effective production of one of the world's most important chemicals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rise of collagen-eating microbes may help explain gaps in the fossil record
item.description: Researchers may have uncovered the reason why some of Earth's earliest animals were commonly preserved as fossils—even though they were essentially fragile "bags of goo"—while later soft-bodied creatures have largely disappeared from the fossil record. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Trump bought up to $25 million in Meta and millions in SpaceX debt in August
item.description: Trump disclosed 517 August trades, including up to $5 million in debt from SpaceX, a major Pentagon contractor and NASA launch provider. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: Harmless amoeba's tight-space crawling offers clues to how its deadly relative invades the brain
item.description: Tiny, shapeless invaders can find their way from ponds to the human brain and cause an infection so severe that it has a 95% fatality rate. The amoeba Naegleria fowleri naturally lives in ponds, feasting on bacteria, but once it enters the human body, it makes a run for the brain tissue, traversing complex, tight spaces to reach its destination. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Seismic analysis reveals ancient traces of mantle flow beneath the Pacific's oldest plate
item.description: Seismic data captured by ocean-bottom instruments have revealed "fossilized" traces of mantle flow beneath the Pacific Ocean's oldest preserved piece of crust. The patterns of ancient flow traced in the uppermost mantle are complicated, tracking changes in tectonic plate motion over time as well as mantle deformation around features such as a sunken remnant of the lithosphere (the crust and the uppermost brittle mantle) and upwelling hotspots. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sea surface temperatures suggest El Niño is strengthening
item.description: Sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific are forecast to increase to record levels during October–December 2026, reflecting the strengthening of the El Niño event, which will drive weather patterns and affect economies, ecosystems and communities across the globe. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Colombia's new bee checklist documents 738 species, including 246 newly recorded
item.description: A team led by a Penn State professor and doctoral student has compiled a checklist documenting the bee species in Colombia—the first of its kind for any country in the Western Hemisphere. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: FDA-approved epilepsy drug may help reverse osteoarthritis damage
item.description: Researchers at Yale have identified a promising new approach to osteoarthritis that could do more than simply ease pain. The epilepsy drug lacosamide appears to block a protein involved in both pain signaling and cartilage destruction, helping damaged joints shift back toward repair in preclinical studies. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: El Reino Unido acusa a un militar de la Royal Navy de espiar para un país extranjero
item.description: Los investigadores desvinculan el caso de Irán y del incidente en la base aérea de Fairford. La BBC señala que su objetivo era pasar información a Rusia Fuente: El País - Internacional.
item.dc:creator: Rafa De Miguel

item.title: Largest 2D map of the universe helps scientists discover new gravitational lenses
item.description: Using data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, with help from artificial intelligence, an international team of scientists has discovered 70 new gravitational lenses—rare cosmic alignments that act as natural magnifying glasses. The new lenses further expand one of the largest collections of confirmed lenses to date and will allow scientists to study dark matter, galaxy evolution and the structure of the universe. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Prepare for the unexpected: The coming super El Niño and NZ's ocean weather
item.description: Residents of Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington know it is always wise to prepare for any weather—to pack sunglasses, a raincoat and at least one extra layer. This "be prepared for anything" approach can equally be applied to Aotearoa's ocean weather during this year's "super" El Niño. Forecasts are fickle, unexpected outcomes are likely and preparation is needed. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists accidentally discover a genetic code that breaks the rules of life
item.description: Scientists accidentally discovered a microscopic organism with a genetic code that breaks a rule researchers thought was nearly universal. While testing a new DNA sequencing technique, they examined a previously unknown protist collected from a freshwater pond at Oxford University. To their surprise, the organism uses two genetic signals that normally mark the end of a gene to encode two entirely different amino acids instead. These signals were previously thought to evolve together, making the discovery particularly remarkable. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Olowalu reef off Maui provides glimpse into two centuries of environmental changes
item.description: New research led by the University of Hawai'i Sea Grant College Program (Hawai'i Sea Grant), the UH Mānoa School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST) and the U.S. Geological Survey analyzed a 253-year-old core from a massive coral colony at Olowalu Reef off West Maui to reconstruct how Olowalu has changed over time, what has driven those changes and what restoring healthy connections between land and sea may mean for the reef's future. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Pottery styles reveal contrasting paths to social complexity in Neolithic Europe
item.description: Societal changes do not follow a linear path—this also holds true for Neolithic Europe, approximately 8,000 to 4,000 years ago. Two researchers from the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine (NASU) and the Leibniz-Zentrum für Archäologie (LEIZA) in Germany have looked at factors driving these dynamics. Using a mathematical model, they analyzed the interplay between population size, production capacity and information exchange. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: This “golden tree” coral was too strange for any known family
item.description: A brilliant yellow coral discovered off Costa Rica proved so unusual that scientists had to create an entirely new family to classify it. The meter-tall colonies rise from seafloors covered in brittle stars, inspiring the Tolkien-inspired name Laurinque elenya, or “golden tree of the stars.” Advanced genetic analysis revealed that the coral belongs to a previously unknown evolutionary lineage. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Study aims to reduce teacher burnout and turnover
item.description: A new study examined how positive psychology interventions could help reduce teacher burnout and turnover, retain valuable knowledge and experience in our schools and create better learning environments for students. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: High-resolution global atmospheric model erases 'popcornlike' rain
item.description: Global climate and weather forecasting use predictive models that divide Earth's atmosphere into a grid, with each section typically covering tens to hundreds of kilometers. Now a new model, run by a team at the University of Tokyo, has narrowed this grid spacing to just 220 meters (720 feet). This higher resolution eliminated instances of "popcornlike" rain—bursts of heavy rain that appear in simulations but not in real life—providing more accurate predictions of extreme local weather from a global model. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists found Homo erectus 200,000 years earlier than expected
item.description: New fossils from South Africa are reshaping the story of early human evolution. Researchers have described 18 hominin fossils from Drimolen Cave, including an adult Homo erectus skull fragment dated to about 2 million years ago, supporting evidence that the species appeared in southern Africa roughly 200,000 years earlier than long thought. The finds also reveal that Paranthropus robustus, which lived alongside Homo erectus, was gradually evolving even larger teeth and stronger chewing muscles as the climate changed. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: DNA testing of fecal samples reveals greater gliders eat wider variety of plants than previously thought
item.description: Identifying the favorite snacks of one of Australia's cutest animals no longer needs to rely on guesswork or picking apart their poop, according to University of the Sunshine Coast research. Although the shortened title of her latest paper is "The future is faeces," associate professor Dominique Potvin and colleagues want to make the task less of a hands-on, hit-and-miss job. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sentinel-3C returns its first views of Earth
item.description: Just two weeks after it was launched, the Copernicus Sentinel-3C satellite returned its first images and measurements from two of its key instruments – a major milestone that confirms the satellite is working well and on the road to monitoring the health of Earth’s oceans, land, cryosphere and atmosphere. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Strong reading skills may help teens resist misinformation
item.description: Students with stronger reading skills are better able to spot misinformation online—and those skills may be especially important for teenagers from disadvantaged backgrounds, according to a new study from the Brown School at Washington University in St. Louis. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA is searching for hidden caves to build its first Moon base
item.description: NASA is preparing for humanity’s first Moon base with three investigations that will hunt for underground shelters, uncover hidden ice, and track dangerous conditions on the lunar surface. The findings could reveal how astronauts can survive and thrive on the Moon while laying the groundwork for future journeys to Mars. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Muere la mujer de la NASA que cambió para siempre lo que significaba ser programador
item.description: Ha muerto a los 90 años Margaret Hamilton, la mujer de la famosa foto de la montaña de folios. Dicha imagen, que ya es todo un icono, es un claro ejemplo de lo que Hamilton supuso para la carrera espacial estadounidense, pero también mundial. Cuando la NASA contrató al MIT en 1961 para desarrollar el sistema de guiado de sus naves, ella era una joven matemática, apenas recién salida de la carrera, que había destacado en el desarrollo de un software de predicción meteorológica cuando la ingeniería de software era apenas una profesión en pañales. Unos años más tarde, ya estaba al mando del… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Brain cells regulate cholesterol to control neuron signaling
item.description: Cholesterol, a fat-like substance in the body best known for its role in cardiovascular health, also plays a key role in how neurons—foundational cells for the brain's ability to process and integrate information—communicate with one another. Now, research led by Vitaly A. Klyachko, a professor in the WashU Medicine Department of Cell Biology & Physiology, has shown that brain cells called astrocytes regulate cholesterol supply to modulate neuronal communication. The findings are published in the Journal of Cell Biology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Electronic stripes linked to unusual vortex states in a superconductor
item.description: Superconductors, materials that can carry electric current with an electrical resistance of zero, have proved to be promising for the development of various technologies, including medical devices, particle accelerators and quantum computers. Studying these materials could help researchers uncover new physical states that could be useful for specific applications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Private equity investments rapidly reshaping CPA firms, creating a gap in accounting education, study finds
item.description: The traditional CPA firm partnership model is undergoing its most rapid transformation in decades. Driven by private equity (PE) investments and acquisitions, public accounting firms are restructuring operations, compensation and career pathways. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Stanford’s 20-year blood-cancer therapy treats first commercial patient; trial found 78% free of GVHD
item.description: In a remarkable advancement, Stanford researchers have unveiled Orca-T therapy, which has recently received FDA approval. After two decades of rigorous development, this innovative treatment was administered to its inaugural commercial patient, a high-risk leukemia sufferer. Notably, Orca-T significantly minimizes the chances of graft-versus-host disease post-stem cell transplants, offering reduced chemotherapy requirements and lower side effects. Future studies are anticipated to investigate its relevance for broader patient demographics. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Mission success: Australian cancer research returns from space
item.description: Human stem cells from Adelaide University's Center for Cancer Biology have successfully traveled to the edge of space and back as part of a landmark mission for Australian cancer research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What pig hearts and a little noise can teach us about designing better soft valves
item.description: Some of the best engineers and inventors are copycats. They look at how the natural world solves complex problems and use those mechanisms as the basis for innovations. But Mother Nature doesn't always give up her secrets easily. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study finds simulation game helps students grasp complex health economics concepts
item.description: In Phillip Zane's classroom, students weigh an invitation to jump out of an airplane. The skydiving lesson and jump are free, and the exercise assumes there is zero risk of death. But an injury could mean $10,000 in medical expenses and $1,000 in lost wages. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: La NASA está preparando un nuevo telescopio para ver lo único que el James Webb es incapaz de ver
item.description: Actualmente, muchos telescopios espaciales están rastreando el cielo de distintas maneras. Tres de los más famosos son el Hubble, el James Webb y el Roman , que partió recientemente hacia su destino. Sin embargo, todos coinciden en una misma carencia: no son capaces de rastrear el cielo midiendo en el infrarrojo lejano. Alrededor de la mitad de la luz emitida por estrellas y galaxias a lo largo de la historia cósmica sale en esta banda del espectro. Por eso, sin un telescopio capaz de medirlo, nos estamos perdiendo la mitad de la fiesta. Afortunadamente, la NASA ya tiene una solución: la… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Einstein Probe reveals a hidden phase of neutron star collisions
item.description: Einstein Probe revealed nearly 10 minutes of soft X-ray activity following a short gamma-ray burst, exposing a phase of neutron star mergers that previous missions may have missed. The prolonged emission could have been powered by a newly formed magnetar and may provide a valuable new counterpart to gravitational-wave signals. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Healthy reef sounds can boost coral and fish recovery efforts
item.description: Coral reefs are renowned for their visual beauty, but for the marine life they support, their sounds may be just as enticing. Two new studies led by UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography reveal how underwater acoustic enrichment—the playback of sounds from healthy reefs—can help spur the recovery of degraded coral reefs and their fish communities. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
item.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms. Publicado también por: European Space Agency. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: As species decline, green turtles offer a glimmer of hope
item.description: The palm-sized green turtle hatchling flailing through the sand on a Malaysian island may seem vulnerable, but its species has emerged as a symbol of hope for wildlife conservation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Margaret Hamilton, scientist who worked on NASA's Apollo program, dead at 90
item.description: American scientist Margaret Hamilton, who led development of the computer system used by NASA's Apollo lunar program, has died at 90, her former employer said Wednesday. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Just 7 days of strength training started shrinking fat cells in mice
item.description: Just seven strength-training sessions helped obese mice shrink visceral fat cells and reactivate molecular pathways involved in burning stored fat, despite no change in overall body weight. The findings suggest some benefits of resistance exercise may begin long before weight loss becomes visible, though the results still need to be confirmed in humans. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Britons kept in dark about scale of climate crisis, say viewers of ‘first-of-its-kind’ emergency briefing
item.description: Nine out of 10 people felt motivated to act after watching film outlining threats to food security, economy and public health The British government must be honest about the scale of the threat posed by climate and nature breakdown, researchers have said, after nine out of 10 people surveyed after watching a briefing on the issue felt more motivated to act. Last November, in the “first-of-its-kind national emergency briefing”, nine experts gave stark assessments in Central Hall in Westminster of the scale of the changes needed in the UK to adapt to the rapidly changing climate and ecological… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Pippa Neill Environment reporter

item.title: Chinese team says its all-in-one mini artificial pancreas offers next-gen diabetes care
item.description: Chinese scientists have created a wearable all-in-one device combining a glucose sensor and insulin micropump that they say paves the way for a fully autonomous mini artificial pancreas, although it has so far only been tested on mice. Unlike existing commercial systems for managing diabetes that typically require patients to wear two separate patches for monitoring and hormone delivery, the new prototype combines both functions in a single coin-sized device. Researchers from the University of... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Bela

item.title: Keeping the sky dark and quiet
item.description: For thousands of years, the night sky has inspired humanity, guided explorers and helped scientists unlock the mysteries of the Universe. As the number of satellites in orbit grows, their reflected light and radio frequency interference become a challenge for both professional astronomy and simple stargazing. The European Space Agency (ESA) and the International Astronomical Union’s Centre for the Protection of the Dark and Quiet Sky (IAU CPS) have signed an agreement at the International Astronautical Congress to strengthen cooperation and develop technical solutions to keep the sky dark and… Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Another NASA crew is coming home. Here's what to expect from their splashdown
item.description: NASA's Crew-12 astronauts are set to parachute back to Earth in a SpaceX capsule, after 237 days of conducting orbital research and lab maintenance on the International Space Station. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Luke Cooper

item.title: University students say procrastination is biggest threat to their academic performance
item.description: More than half of US students surveyed said the problem damaged their ability to do academic work, study finds Procrastination is the biggest problem that can harm students’ academic performance at university, according to a study of more than 65,000 young people who placed it above issues such as ADHD, anxiety or financial worries. The study found that nearly half of the students surveyed named procrastination as the thing damaging their ability to do academic work, more than twice the number who named depression, while the same proportion said procrastination caused them significant… Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Richard Adams Education editor

item.title: Margaret Hamilton, whose software helped land Apollo 11 on the Moon, dies at 90
item.description: Pioneering computer scientist led the development of the software for Nasa's Apollo mission and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: Scientists warn a popular vitamin D supplement may have a hidden downside
item.description: Not all vitamin D supplements are created equal, and new research suggests that one popular form may have an unexpected downside. Scientists found that taking vitamin D2 can actually lower the body's levels of vitamin D3, the form naturally produced by sunlight and more effective at boosting overall vitamin D. Previous studies also suggest that vitamin D3 may provide stronger immune protection against viruses and bacteria. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The Saturn […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Fighting Drought in Texas Cotton Country
item.description: Drought and an ailing aquifer were major topics of conversation when NASA scientists visited with farmers in the Texas High Plains. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Working around men may make women feel worse about mistakes, study finds
item.description: We all make them, and we all make them at work: Mistakes on the job happen regardless of line of work, experience or gender. How employees feel about them and how they are perceived by others, however, differs. Women are more likely than men to perceive mistakes negatively—but this depends on whom they share the office with, a new study in Frontiers in Organizational Psychology has shown. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Not all trans fats are bad, major review finds
item.description: A large analysis of 22 studies found that the trans fats naturally present in dairy foods such as milk, butter, yogurt, and cheese do not appear to raise the risk of heart disease or type 2 diabetes. Unlike industrial trans fats from partially hydrogenated oils, dairy trans fats showed no meaningful harmful effects on blood fats in controlled trials and were not linked to higher rates of heart disease, stroke, cardiovascular death, or diabetes in long-term studies. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Listening to hidden insects could give farmers an early warning of crop pests
item.description: Crawling through muddy soybean fields to inspect several plant-mounted microphones was not on Emily Sur's graduate school bingo card, but she's not mad about it. Her research offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of entomology, agriculture and emerging technologies while still doing what she loves. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI chatbots endorse existing climate-related policies twice as often as new proposals
item.description: A new study of multiple large language models (LLMs) found that when users asked chatbots for advice, the chatbots were more likely to make suggestions that favor the status quo over alternatives. The tendency of artificial intelligence to default to more common advice could be bad news for the climate. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dads are dying after their kids are born, and almost no one is tracking it
item.description: A study of more than 130,000 babies born in Georgia found that hundreds of fathers died within the first five years of their child’s life, and about 60% of those deaths were potentially preventable. Homicide, accidental injuries, suicide, and drug overdoses accounted for most of the preventable deaths, highlighting what researchers call a major blind spot in public health. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Cross-border shopping dilutes public revenue less than previously thought
item.description: Will higher sin taxes, and therefore higher prices, on candy, soft drinks and beer lead to more cross-border shopping? The answer is often assumed to be yes in the public debate, where one of the main arguments against sin taxes on unhealthy products has long been that higher prices will encourage more Danes to shop across the border. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Emotional ties to cultural heritage show strongest link to digital museum engagement
item.description: Museums are increasingly using digital technologies to create more interactive and accessible experiences for visitors. Technologies such as three-dimensional (3D) digital models, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) allow visitors to explore artifacts in new ways, both online and during visits to physical museums. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Digital finance research maps psychology, algorithms, and risk
item.description: A study of almost 1,000 research papers in the field of digital finance has mapped out how technology, investor behavior and financial market risk are connected. The work identified three distinct foundations rather than a single framework, with implications for understanding how psychological factors influence financial decisions and how to develop viable algorithms that provide automated investment guidance. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rising seas threaten the world's migratory shorebirds
item.description: Birds undertake some of the world's most impressive migrations, traveling hundreds to thousands of kilometers every year in search of safe breeding grounds and seasonally abundant food resources. For many birds, migration is the key to their success. However, migration can also make species more vulnerable to threats. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Artemis III: uno de los astronautas convocados reveló por qué no hay mujeres la misión
item.description: El astronauta de la Agencia Espacial Europea es uno de los cuatro integrantes de la nueva delegación; bromeó con la posibilidad de llevar comida de su país al espacio Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Stanford scientists turn a cancer driver into a kill switch
item.description: A Stanford-designed molecule turns a major lymphoma-promoting protein against cancer cells, activating their own self-destruct machinery instead of simply blocking tumor growth. In mice, the treatment completely eliminated aggressive human lymphoma tumors within 11 days, although much more testing is needed before it could reach patients. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Five ways to enjoy fashion as a hobby without indulging in overconsumption
item.description: Fashion lovers are generally associated with bursting wardrobes and chasing the latest trends. But that reputation is beginning to shift. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How Spain's torrential rainstorms put sewage into its rivers and seas
item.description: After heavy rain, Spanish cities often awaken to refreshed air and clean streets, while the rainwater itself vanishes into storm drains along with everything it swept away. Underground, however, a very different story unfolds. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Snowball Earth's iron deposits may have formed through microbes living without sunlight
item.description: Iron is one of the most abundant metals on Earth's surface, yet how such massive iron ore deposits formed throughout geological history has long remained a mystery. The prevailing theory has been that ancient photosynthetic bacteria oxidized iron, causing it to precipitate and accumulate in the oceans. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: From jargon to impact: Teaching undergraduates the art of public communication
item.description: Articles published in The Conversation go well beyond academics writing for a general audience—they can also serve as valuable content for educators to use in the classroom. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Woody ‘blankets’ deployed on Arctic permafrost to reduce carbon emissions
item.description: Nature, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03045-8 A start-up company is testing whether stabilizing areas of rapidly eroding permafrost can prevent greenhouse-gas emissions. Fuente: Nature.

item.title: UAE completes Arab world's first solo space probe – and sets course for an asteroid
item.description: Nature, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03154-4 The device will be launched on a joint UAE-US-built craft. Some researchers say it could be the last mission constructed with outside help. Fuente: Nature.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Gibney

item.title: Tiny photosynthetic organisms help transport carbon to the depths of the Baltic Sea
item.description: Tiny photosynthetic organisms in the Baltic Sea can contribute substantially to the transport of carbon from surface waters to deeper parts of the sea. A new study from the Department of Ecology, Environment and Plant Sciences at Stockholm University shows that their ability to form colonies and aggregates is an important factor determining how much of their biomass sinks. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Artemis II crew moon photo annotations
item.description: A visualization of a dark Moon eclipsing the Sun is marked with handwritten notes in this April 6, 2026, screenshot from an Artemis II crew member’s tablet. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (in blue) and Victor “Ike” Glover (in green) and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) Jeremy Hansen (in red) observed impact flashes and their locations, which […] Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How a harmful bacterium senses iron—and why it matters for fighting infections
item.description: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a common culprit in hospital-acquired bacterial infections and is growing more resistant to antibiotics. New findings from Aaron Smith, professor of chemistry and biochemistry at UMBC, and collaborators at Oklahoma State University show how a two-protein system inside the bacterium operates like a sensitive switch: The pair detects iron both outside and inside the cell and then rewrites large parts of the microbe's metabolism in response. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: International experience gives business leaders an edge, study finds
item.description: Business leaders with international experience play a significant role in shaping the success of their organizations and are often associated with stronger organizational performance, including higher growth, profitability and stock market performance, according to a new study published in the Journal of Management. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Superbug P. aeruginosa uses two protein plugs to seal channels against antibiotics
item.description: A joint research team has identified a new mechanism underlying antibiotic resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a major multidrug-resistant "superbug." The discovery provides important clues for the development of new treatments for multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. The findings are published in the journal Nature Communications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chain reaction that begins when tumor suppression gene is switched off offers clues to how cancer develops
item.description: A tumor suppressor gene known as p53 is mutated in more than half of all cancers, but how it acts to prevent cancer formation is largely unknown. A study by UT Southwestern Medical Center researchers sheds light on this phenomenon by showing what happens when p53 becomes disabled, revealing the gene's diverse roles in maintaining healthy metabolic activity, repressing mobile genes called retrotransposons and preventing cells from adopting features of sperm and eggs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nobel physics winner's pride at pioneering AI role
item.description: Francis Halzen, winner of the Nobel Prize in physics, spoke with pride on Wednesday about his early promotion of artificial intelligence in his research on neutrinos. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Offshore wind turbine foundations may cool ocean surface by mixing seawater
item.description: New research within the PELAgIO ECOWind project has revealed how offshore wind farms can influence ocean temperatures and mixing, and why their effects depend on local conditions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Survey finds K-12 educators self-censor to avoid controversy over book selections
item.description: Elementary school teachers often put such care into creating their classroom libraries: shelving multiple copies of each book, stringing lights around them to set the mood, situating beanbag chairs and magic carpet squares strategically to encourage students to settle in. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NYC congestion pricing policy linked to cleaner air in lower Manhattan
item.description: One year after New York City launched its congestion pricing policy, fine particulate pollution inside Manhattan's congestion relief zone was 13% lower, according to a new analysis that accounted for regional pollution trends, weather and normal year-to-year variability. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: First-in-kind data set reveals insights across the world's national and regional economies
item.description: The University of Virginia has published the Global Capitalism Index (GCI), a first-in-kind data set offering unprecedented insights into the globe's capitalism conditions in every country. Assembled from more than two hundred data sets across eight key pillars, the GCI's country-by-country scores offer an array of ways to understand capitalism around the world. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Long Island measurements reveal household products and buildings as major summer pollution sources
item.description: Products such as hairspray, paint and household disinfectants are increasingly causing summertime air pollution—and cities aren't accounting for it, which makes it harder to issue air quality advisories and enact regulations, new research from Colorado State University, the University of Minnesota and Purdue University shows. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hawaiian hot spot study uncovers evidence of true polar wander
item.description: On Earth, everything is moving. The planet spins, the tectonic plates shift and the spin axis wobbles, as do the magnetic poles, which makes determining how things move a rather tricky proposition. For Rice University's Richard Gordon, this problem came up when he was trying to understand the history of the Hawaiian hot spot, the deep-mantle source of the volcanism that created the Hawaiian–Emperor chain of islands and underwater volcanoes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Eight-year analysis reveals how sunlight and nutrients shape sustainable urban farming
item.description: Factors such as sunlight and stage-specific nutrient application determine crop success in urban agriculture, far beyond fixed recipes or miracle solutions. The findings are published in the journal Agronomy for Sustainable Development. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Self-blinking dyes' simplify nanoscale imaging without sacrificing precision
item.description: Nanobodies are extremely small antibody fragments that bind to specific molecules. When nanobodies are labeled with dyes, they can be used as probes to enhance super-resolution microscopy. However, conventional blinking dyes often perform poorly when attached to nanobodies, limiting their practical advantages. An international research team led by the University of Göttingen and the University Medical Center Göttingen (UMG) has now shown that self-blinking dyes—which can switch between bright and dark states on their own—bypass this limitation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sharks’ Long-Range Hearing: Study finds 74m sound detection; sharks turn away
item.description: A team of researchers from Florida Atlantic University discovered that wild blacktip sharks possess the ability to detect low-frequency sounds from considerable distances. This groundbreaking study sheds light on how these sharks navigate their aquatic environments, as they exhibited keen directional hearing by making sharp turns in response to sound sources. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Undergraduate student may have solved puzzle regarding isolated galaxies that have stopped producing stars
item.description: An undergraduate astrophysics student at UC Berkeley has found three unusual galaxies—cataloged as Shapiro Dwarf Galaxies I, II and III. Each galaxy is far from other galaxies and has stopped making stars, a combination that is extremely rare. The discovery, published in The Astrophysical Journal, provides compelling observational evidence of a long-held astronomical theory. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New approach to plant stress studies could yield hardier crops and medical insights
item.description: At the University of Missouri, plant scientist Ron Mittler is rewriting the playbook for how scientists study life by asking what happens when living organisms face multiple stresses at once. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Sets Coverage for SpaceX 35th Station Resupply Launch, Arrival
item.description: NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT, Tuesday, Oct. 13, for the next launch to deliver science investigations, supplies, and equipment, including the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays, to the space station. This is the 35th SpaceX commercial resupply services mission to the orbital complex for NASA. NASA also will […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: New polystyrene uses 50% plant-based material and breaks into fragments for potential recycling
item.description: Polystyrene is used in protective packaging for televisions and electronic devices, in decorative boards and baseboards for interior construction, and in petri dishes. It is one of the world's most important plastics, with nearly 20 million tons produced each year. The material is predominantly derived from crude oil and is rarely recycled. Virgin polystyrene is often cheaper than recycled material, meaning that used products are typically incinerated or sent to landfills. Like many other plastics, polystyrene is highly resistant to degradation in the environment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ultrashort laser pulses let new microscope map electron interactions across thin materials
item.description: A new type of advanced microscope (wide-field coherent multidimensional microscopy) has been developed. It uses a carefully designed sequence of ultrashort light pulses to study the behavior of high-tech materials, with potential practical applications in the study of innovative materials such as those used to build solar panels. This is the result of work by a research group of physicists from the Faculty of Sciences, Mathematics, Physics, and Natural Sciences at Università Cattolica's Brescia campus who, for the first time, have developed a "multidimensional microscope" that, in a sense… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ebola creates new hot spots in Congo as responders describe 'chaotic' response
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in Congo is creating new hot spots where there's little to no support for patients, responders and officials say, as health workers admit there could still be a long way to go in fighting the disease that has killed over 4,000 people. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: First global genome atlas reveals overlooked microscopic life in hundreds of lakes and reservoirs
item.description: Tiny single-celled organisms help keep lakes clear, but some can also contaminate the water. An international research team has analyzed DNA data from 362 lakes to create the first global genome atlas of these organisms. With the findings now published in Nature Communications, the new atlas lays the foundation for faster and more precise monitoring of lakes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tiny plasma-grown particles enable easier magnetization reversal in materials for high-frequency electronics
item.description: Researchers at South China University of Technology, in collaboration with the Dongguan Institute of Materials Science and Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, have developed a novel supranano multi-precipitate microstructure in amorphous soft magnetic composites using Ar/O₂ plasma treatment. By facilitating magnetic-moment reversal, this approach significantly reduced coercivity while maintaining excellent overall performance. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Giant tortoises outnumber people in Seychelles, with nearly 183,000 on Aldabra
item.description: A landmark survey of the world's largest free-roaming giant tortoise population has revealed that the once-endangered species is thriving and stable in the Seychelles. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Acoustic experiments confirm topology can persist at gapless critical points
item.description: Two studies on critical topology have recently been published in the journal Nature. These studies were led by the teams of Prof. Baile Zhang at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, and Prof. Jianhua Jiang at the University of Science and Technology of China, respectively. Prof. Xue-Jia Yu from the School of Physics at the Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo (EIT), served as a co-corresponding author on both papers and provided key theoretical guidance in the related experimental collaborations. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New display technology combines record brightness with pixels that stretch like rubber
item.description: A research team led by Professor Jiwoong Yang of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering at DGIST has developed the world's first foundational technology for an ultrahigh-resolution stretchable quantum dot display (QLED) that can stretch freely like skin while maintaining sharp image quality. The findings were published in Nature Nanotechnology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Use of natural gas or propane in commercial kitchens exposes workers to air pollution and dangerous heat
item.description: Restaurant workers in commercial kitchens with gas and propane appliances can face heat and air pollution at levels above health-based guidelines, according to a new study by researchers from PSE Healthy Energy, the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability and New York University Grossman School of Medicine, in collaboration with chef Christopher Galarza. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Using AI for feedback, not ready-made answers, may help students earn higher grades
item.description: Although the use of AI may improve students' performance on average, what matters more is how students use it. If students use AI instrumentally, their grades may even be lower than those of students who do not use AI at all. By contrast, using AI to seek feedback and identify missing perspectives may lead to significantly better performance than other approaches to AI use. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Coach training leaves gaps in addressing girls' and women's needs in sport
item.description: "There is a systemic failure in the training of coaches for female athletes," says Ådne Ausland, a researcher at the University of Agder. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Flexible tails could boost ancient sea predators' ambush speeds, fossil-based models suggest
item.description: Some of the giant marine reptiles that ruled the seas during the age of dinosaurs were better built for surprise attacks, while their relatives were better suited to chasing prey through open water, according to a Rutgers-led study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cutting unnecessary tasks shows surprising links to greater employee exhaustion
item.description: Ahead of World Mental Health Day on Oct. 10, attention is turning to the question of what causes psychological strain at work. A study by Bielefeld University shows that inappropriate tasks are not the only factor associated with exhaustion. Changes in day-to-day work can also leave employees feeling exhausted, even when the number of burdensome tasks decreases. Perceived uncertainty plays an important role. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Noah’s Ark mystery deepens as archaeologists drill Mount Ararat site for ancient wood clues
item.description: Archaeologists investigating Turkey’s Mount Ararat have drilled the boat-shaped Durupinar formation for the first time, collecting hundreds of soil samples from depths of up to 60 feet. Researchers are examining organic matter and possible traces of ancient wood for clues linked to Noah’s Ark, but laboratory analysis is still needed before drawing conclusions. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Polymer coating tackles MXene's water stability challenge, boosting CO₂-to-methane production
item.description: A research team has developed a photocatalytic technology that improves the stability of MXene, an emerging material vulnerable to water, to efficiently convert carbon dioxide into methane. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Radio galaxy from 12.5 billion years ago may be most powerful ever found
item.description: Astronomers have confirmed a powerful radio galaxy from nearly 12.5 billion years ago. The source, TXS 2354+015, was originally identified as a high-redshift candidate from its characteristic drop in optical light, and follow-up spectroscopy placed it at a redshift of 4.946. Their paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 23. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Enzymes could unlock biological recycling of difficult plastic waste
item.description: They are durable, cheap and everyday life is now hardly imaginable without them: plastics. More then 400 million metric tons are produced every year. As a large proportion is only insufficiently recycled, the environmental burden caused by plastic waste is increasing. Fuente: Phys.org.
